methodologyNotes: Roster covers twelve battery- and AC-powered studio/location strobes spanning budget Bowens-mount monolights (Neewer Vision4, Godox SK400II, Interfit Honey Badger 320) to professional battery-powered all-in-ones (Godox AD600Pro/AD400Pro, Profoto B10 Plus, Elinchrom ELB 500 TTL, Westcott FJ400, Flashpoint XPLOR 600 Pro) and AC-only industrial units (Paul C. Buff Einstein E640, Broncolor Siros 400 S, Godox QT600IIM), verified 2026-08-09 primarily against manufacturer spec pages (godox.com, fjwestcott.com, us.elinchrom.com, broncolor.swiss, Paul C. Buff's own product page) and corroborated by major retailers (B&H, Adorama, Newegg, Amazon) via search-result snippets where direct page fetches were blocked by bot protection (B&H and Adorama both returned HTTP 403 on nearly every direct fetch attempt in this session); several fields are left null rather than guessed where no fetched source stated a figure (e.g. modeling-lamp wattage for the Elinchrom ELB 500 TTL and Paul C. Buff Einstein E640, both of which do not publish a watt rating for their lamps), and priceUsd is left null with an explanatory priceNote for the Flashpoint XPLOR 600 Pro, Interfit Honey Badger 320, Neewer Vision4, and Godox QT600IIM, where every attempted US retailer product page returned an access-blocked response and only stale, non-US, or bundle-inclusive price figures could be found. Two naming notes mirroring real market conditions rather than errors: the Godox AD600Pro and AD400Pro entries describe the original (non-"II") SKUs per the requested seed names, even though Godox has since released AD600Pro II/AD400Pro II successors that are now the primary items on godox.com; and the Godox SK400II entry describes the currently-sold "SK400II-V" hardware revision (10W LED modeling lamp, 5700K), since the original halogen-lamp SK400II this name once referred to is discontinued and every current retailer now sells and lists the V revision simply as "SK400II." accessedAt 2026-08-09 throughout.

products.name: Godox AD600Pro 600Ws TTL Outdoor Flash
products.priceNote: B&H Photo list price (frequently discounted to ~$799). Godox has since released the AD600Pro II successor, but the original AD600Pro remains sold new by Godox and major retailers.

specs.flash_duration_t01: 1/220 to 1/11760 sec (up to ~1/20000 sec in Freeze/Multi-Freeze mode)
specs.ttl_hss_support: TTL (Canon E-TTL II, Nikon i-TTL, Sony, Fujifilm, Olympus, Panasonic); HSS to 1/8000s
specs.power_source: Removable 28.8V/2600mAh lithium-ion battery (up to 360 full-power flashes); optional AC adapter

products.provenance: Godox's own AD600Pro product page confirms 600Ws output, built-in 2.4G X wireless system, and lithium battery power. Flash duration (1/220-1/11760 sec), recycle time (0.01-0.9s), and 38W/4800K LED modeling lamp figures cross-checked against B&H's product listing and a Godox modeling-lamp replacement-part listing (ML-AD600PRO). Battery spec (28.8V/2600mAh, 360 full-power flashes) confirmed via multiple Amazon listings reproducing Godox's own spec sheet. Price ($899) is B&H's current list price; B&H frequently runs a $100 instant-savings promotion bringing it to ~$799.

specs.ttl_hss_support: TTL (Canon, Nikon, Sony, Fujifilm, Olympus); HSS to 1/8000s
specs.power_source: Removable 21.6V/2600mAh lithium-ion battery (up to 390 full-power flashes); optional AC adapter

specs.flash_duration_t01: as fast as 1/50000 sec in Freeze mode; 1/3400 sec best case in Normal mode

LED modeling-light specs (150W-equivalent, 2500 lm max, 3000-6500K ±500K, 90-96 CRI) and battery figures (up to 200 full-power flashes, sub-90-minute charge) corroborated across KelbyOne's hands-on review and Capture Integration's comparison page, both of which cite Profoto's published spec sheet directly.

specs.flash_duration_t01: 1/220 to 1/11760 sec (up to ~1/20400 sec in Freeze mode)
specs.ttl_hss_support: Manual only on this SKU (Flashpoint R2 2.4GHz radio system); HSS to 1/8000s. A separate TTL SKU (XPLOR 600 PRO TTL) is sold for specific camera mounts.

Flash duration and recycle-time figures carried over from the identical underlying Godox AD600Pro platform (1/220-1/11760 sec, 0.01-0.9s) per SLR Lounge's hands-on review of the same hardware.

products.name: Elinchrom ELB 500 TTL Power Pack & Head
products.priceNote: Price for the ELB 500 TTL pack-and-head unit alone, per Elinchrom-authorized dealer listings. Complete 'To Go' kits with case, stand, and extra battery run $1,900-$2,125; a 2-head bundle listing was seen as high as $2,749.95.

specs.flash_duration_t01: as fast as 1/20000 sec in Action mode; 1/3400 sec best case in Normal mode
specs.ttl_hss_support: TTL (Canon, Nikon, Sony via Elinchrom EL-Skyport); HSS to 1/8000s
specs.power_source: Removable 14.4V/5Ah (72Wh) lithium-ion battery (up to 400 full-power flashes, supports charging while in use); AC input 100-240V, 50/60Hz

products.provenance: Elinchrom's US site confirms 500Ws max power (7Ws min, 7 f-stop range), TTL and HSS to 1/8000s, 20-channel/4-group 2.4GHz wireless, and the 72Wh li-ion battery rated for 400 full-power flashes with active charging support. Recycle time (2 sec at max power) and best-case flash duration (1/20000 sec Action mode, per DPReview's launch coverage and Elinchrom's own spec sheet) fill out the 0.05-2s and duration ranges. Neither Elinchrom's site nor the fetched B&H/DPReview pages publish a modeling-lamp wattage or the LED's color temperature, so both are left null rather than estimated. Standalone unit price ($1,249.95) per lens-camera.com/authorized-dealer listing corroborated against the $1,900-$2,125 'To Go' kit pricing on DPReview and B&H.

products.name: Paul C. Buff Einstein E640 Flash Unit
products.priceNote: Current price via lens-camera.com, an authorized Paul C. Buff reseller; Paul C. Buff sells primarily direct-to-consumer with no significant third-party retail markup.

specs.flash_duration_t01: 1/568 sec at full power (Constant Color mode, t0.5 1/1600 sec); as fast as ~1/2000 sec (t0.1) at half power in Action Mode
specs.ttl_hss_support: Manual only — no TTL, no camera-side HSS. Fires via CyberSync radio triggers or optical slave; Action Mode shortens flash duration for motion-freezing rather than providing sync-pulse HSS.
specs.power_source: AC only (100-240V, 3-wire grounded, auto-sensing with IEC connector); no battery option

products.provenance: Paul C. Buff's own Einstein E640 product page (hosted at their onlinehome.us domain) confirms the 9 f-stop power range (640Ws full to 2.5Ws at 1/256, adjustable in 1/10-stop increments) and 1.7-second full-power recycle time that scales down proportionally at lower power. The Einstein's own hosted user manual (via ManualsLib) confirms color temperature is held to 5600K ±50K in Constant Color mode across the entire power range (rising to ~5750K at half power in Action Mode), full-power t.5 flash duration of 1/1600 sec and t.1 of 1/568 sec, ~1/2000 sec t.1 at half power in Action Mode, and AC-only 3-wire grounded power with no battery option. No fetched source publishes a modeling-lamp wattage rating (the manual describes adjustable Proportional/Manual/Off modeling-light modes without a watt figure), so modeling_lamp_w is left null rather than guessed. Price $529.95 per lens-camera.com, an authorized reseller.

products.name: Interfit Honey Badger 320Ws Compact Flash Head
products.priceNote: B&H, Samy's, Adorama, and Interfit's own product pages all returned access-blocked (403/404) responses on every direct fetch attempted in this session, so no single-head price could be independently verified. A B&H listing for the Honey Badger 320Ws 2-Light Kit was found at $769.99 list ($498.99 sale), but halving a 2-light kit price to estimate a single head would be a guess, so priceUsd is left null rather than inferred.

specs.ttl_hss_support: Manual only — no TTL, no HSS documented in the manufacturer manual (fires via built-in optical slave or 2.4G radio trigger accessories)
specs.power_source: AC power port (no battery option); optional external battery packs sold separately by Interfit

products.provenance: Interfit's own instruction manual for the Honey Badger (hosted on ManualsLib) confirms 320Ws max power, 7 f-stop range in 1/10-stop increments, GN 148 (100 ISO, 1/125, 1m, 7in reflector), 1/900 sec flash duration and 1 second recycle time at full power, an LED modeling lamp, and an AC power port, but does not document TTL/HSS capability or a modeling-lamp wattage figure. BorrowLenses' rental spec sheet independently corroborates the 320Ws power, 1/900 sec duration, 1-second recycle time, and additionally states a 60W LED modeling lamp and 5600K±200K color-stable output, filling in the two gaps left by the manual. No pricing was locatable on any directly-fetchable source.

products.name: Neewer Vision4 300W Battery-Powered Studio Strobe
products.priceNote: Neewer.com's dedicated product page 404'd on direct fetch and B&H/Amazon listing pages either blocked the request (403) or omitted the dynamically-loaded price field, so no current USD figure could be confirmed without guessing. Neewer Vision4 kits (with trigger and softbox/umbrella) have historically retailed in the $280-$400 range at B&H, but that range was not independently re-verified in this session.

specs.ttl_hss_support: Manual only — does not support TTL or HSS. Native sync speed capped at 1/200 sec; fires via Manual, Multi, or built-in 2.4G wireless remote modes.
specs.power_source: Removable 10.8V/7800mAh lithium-ion battery (up to 1000 full-power flashes)

products.provenance: NeweggBusiness's Vision4 listing confirms 300W power, explicitly states the unit does NOT support TTL and HSS modes, documents flash duration of 1/1000-1/10000 sec, 0.4-2.5s recycle time, GN60 (1m ISO100), the 13W LED modeling lamp, and the 10.8V/7800mAh removable lithium battery rated for up to 1000 full-power flashes (reconciling with an alternate figure of 700 flashes cited elsewhere as a possibly more conservative sustained-use rating). Amazon's listing title independently corroborates the Bowens-mount, 300W, li-ion, 2.4G-wireless, 0.4-2.5s-recycle description. Color temperature (5600K±200K) is the figure consistently cited across retailer listing copy though not independently re-confirmed on a directly fetched Neewer-controlled source.

products.name: Godox QT600IIM 600Ws Studio Flash Monolight
products.priceNote: Every US retailer product page attempted (B&H, Amazon) returned an access-blocked or server-error response on direct fetch. The only price located was €408.99 on Fotoconic, a European retailer, which is not a valid US MSRP and was not converted/used as one. No US price is asserted rather than guessed from the EU figure.

specs.flash_duration_t01: 1/316 sec at minimum power to 1/4246 sec at maximum power
specs.ttl_hss_support: Manual only — no camera TTL; supports High-Speed Sync (HSS) to 1/8000s via Godox 2.4G X-series wireless triggers, plus a Stable Color Mode

products.provenance: Godox's own user manual, hosted and machine-indexed at manua.ls, states 600Ws max power, 0.05s (min) to 0.9s (max) recycle time, flash duration from 1/316 sec (min power) to 1/4246 sec (max power), a 150W modeling lamp bulb, 5600K color temperature, 110-220V AC input, Bowens mount, and built-in Godox X-series 2.4G wireless compatibility. Fotoconic's retail listing independently corroborates the 600Ws rating, AC-only design, and X-series wireless system, and separately documents the unit's High-Speed Sync and Stable Color Mode features (manual-trigger HSS, not camera TTL/HSS). One Amazon listing claims an alternate, much shorter flash duration of 1/19606 sec, which appears to be either a different measurement convention (t0.5 vs t0.1) or marketing copy not corroborated by Godox's own manual; the manual's 1/316-1/4246 sec figures are used as the more authoritative source.

A Newegg listing corroborates the 400W rating, 0.02-1.4s recycle time (a slightly wider range than Broncolor's own 0.02-0.95s figure, likely reflecting a different measured voltage/config), and additionally states 5750K color temperature, not published on Broncolor's own spec page. US price ($2,263.95) taken from the Newegg/authorized-dealer listing; Broncolor's own page lists only the €1,612.00 ex-VAT European MSRP.

products.name: Godox SK400II 400Ws Studio Flash Monolight
products.priceNote: Current Newegg listing price for the hardware currently sold as "SK400II" (technically the SK400II-V revision — see note below).

specs.flash_duration_t01: documented only as an approximate 1/800-1/2000 sec range across retailer listings; not explicitly labeled t0.1 vs t0.5 in any fetched source
specs.ttl_hss_support: Manual only — no TTL, no genuine camera-side HSS (Bowens-mount studio monolight synced via Godox 2.4G X-series wireless trigger; some retailer copy advertises a nominal '1/8000s' figure that appears to describe trigger sync ceiling rather than verified true HSS)

products.provenance: NAMING NOTE: the original Godox SK400II (halogen modeling lamp, GN65, ~0.4-3s recycle) has been superseded by the SK400II-V revision (10W LED modeling lamp, touch-friendlier controls, faster 0.1-1.5s recycle), and B&H, Amazon, and Newegg all currently list and sell the V revision simply as "Godox SK400II" or "SK400II-V" interchangeably — mirroring how JET's JBG-8A/JBG-8B naming works in the bench-grinders dataset. This entry documents the currently-sold V-revision hardware. Newegg's listing confirms 400Ws power, 5700K±200K color-stable output, Bowens mount, 0.1-1.5s recycle time, the 10W LED modeling lamp (5-100% adjustable), built-in Godox 2.4G X-series wireless, and up to 1000 full-power shots; price $329.77. B&H's SK400II-V product page corroborates the model naming and Bowens-mount/LED-modeling-lamp specification. No fetched source gave an unambiguous t0.1 flash-duration figure (only a loosely-labeled 1/800-1/2000 sec range appears across older SK400II retailer copy), so that field is presented with an explicit caveat rather than a false-precision number.
